findings.title: Choice-host install silently drops the CLI offline posture
findings.observed: The early choice_host branch calls choices::run(ctx, &args), dropping root_offline and bypassing normal prepare/direct offline resolution. choices::run never consumes args.offline or the environment/config ladder. ChoiceOperation has no caller offline binding; ConfigurationChoiceHost Prepare uses self.install.clone() at configuration_choice.rs418–424.
findings.consequence: An invocation that explicitly requests offline can reach an online-configured trusted host and execute the ordinary normalized source transaction/acquisition under the host online posture. This violates the existing CLI offline boundary, even though semantic selections/default receipts remain valid.
findings.source_contract: crates/vibe-cli/src/cli.rs143–154 documents resolution/fetch entirely offline; cli/pkg.rs54–67 and commands/install/direct.rs85–86 preserve the normal effective ladder.
findings.reproduction_inference: Use an admitted online-configured ConfigurationChoiceHost (InstallRequest.offline=false), then the ordinary CLI --offline choice-host prepare path with explicit shown/default permission and a selected source needing acquisition. Client offline is neither transmitted nor checked. No network experiment was run.
findings.minimal_fix: Preserve the effective caller offline posture at the choice entry/host preparation boundary, or refuse a posture mismatch before source preparation/acquisition. Continue using the same host/source owner; do not add a planner or universal lifecycle.
findings.verification_gap: Current shared fixture makes InstallRequest.offline=true and CLI direct test passes true, so all retained positives have compatible offline state and cannot detect this loss. Add one bounded arm to existing CLI/service family with an online-capable counting/refusing source to prove caller offline is preserved or rejected before source work; no broad suite required.
